Measured: of the four test files the three pins cite, only tests/test_documented_claims.py opens a pin (Fetched:, Source:, and one anchored > quote in cc-hook-protocol.md); test_hook_protocol, test_nested_repo_litter and test_hook_exec_form name the pins only in comments and test espalier code, so their result cannot depend on upstream text. Running them with the candidate standing in for the pin would verify at most one sentence of one pin, and a raw candidate page has no Fetched: line, so that one test would red on every run. Meanwhile the anchored sentence ("Exit 2's block is the one outcome JSON can't override") is gone from the 2026-10-10 hooks page (the meaning survives as "they can't override the block"), and the test is green only because it reads the committed pin. Design: (1) drift becomes a quote check -- each pin's > passages checked against the fetched page (links and markup normalised, elisions split), the moved passages named by line, none when every quote stands; it replaces the whole-body diff. (2) bound tests derived from each pin body unioned with the two current files, pinned by one test, run on the committed tree and reported as "espalier's claims still hold", not "upstream verified". (3) no candidate-stands-in run: the quote check is the candidate check. (4) proof: re-verify all three pins -- a full re-excerpt of the hooks pin (12 moved passages, the anchor among them; the test's anchor moves with it) -- then gh workflow enable refresh-externals.yml. Shipped runtime, full tier. Starts once #175 (job 2) merges or stacked on it.
